# Application design and units of work

This design belongs to original execution task `4efa3315-df53-4a8b-a935-fbc7ba0bacac`, with Raunak Poonia as the named developer. It creates no replacement task and authorizes no execution during planning. The deliverable is a scoped, open, unmerged PR remediating CVE-2026-90711 / GHSA-jqcg-44mw-7w3h through proxy-addr 2.0.7 → 2.0.8, with fresh compatibility, regression, CI, vulnerability and usage evidence. Retain the other 49 findings as open.

## Repository grounding

Read-only inspection confirmed HEAD `dff02375d83394d6f03ce2127e35e62fadc269ab`. Read `package.json`, the relevant Express and proxy-addr entries of `package-lock.json`, all of `src/server.js`, all five existing test files, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.eslintrc.json` and `.eslintignore`.

The lockfile resolves proxy-addr 2.0.7 through Express's `~2.0.7` requirement. The application has no trust-proxy setting. Existing tests use Node's test runner, local HTTP servers and controlled Axios mocks; static expansion gives 9 health + 8 freshness + 14 service-health + 15 promo-code + 3 smoke cases = 49. The CI workflow uses Node 20, `npm ci`, `npm run lint` and `npm test`. These are file observations, not execution results. No tests, installations, scans, network requests or mutations occurred.

Only the primary repository was inspected. Selected context documents and supplied attachment references are empty; no omitted context is listed. PR106, AXM-707, the live advisory and release contents remain unverified execution references. Runtime-owned checkout and attachment receipts are not manufactured by this document.

## Components

| Component | State and paths | Design responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dependency resolution | Existing, changed: `package-lock.json`; existing, conditional change: `package.json` | Prefer updating only proxy-addr's locked version, resolved artifact and integrity metadata. Express's existing range admits 2.0.8. Preserve unrelated versions and overrides; change the manifest only if demonstrated necessary. |
| Security regression | Proposed: `test/proxy-addr.test.js` | Four Node test cases, S1/S2/C1/C2, exercising the installed dependency under the verified advisory precondition. Use strict assertions and independently justified expectations. |
| Application | Existing, verification only: `src/server.js` | Preserve default disabled trust proxy, dashboard and promo-code routes, metrics, health responses, 2000 ms timeout and recovery. No production configuration change. |
| Compatibility suite | Existing, verification only: `test/health.test.js`, `test/health-freshness.test.js`, `test/service-health.test.js`, `test/promo-codes.test.js`, `test/smoke.test.js` | Run all 49 existing cases before changes and as part of the final suite. Preserve current assertions, mocks and security floors. |
| Hosted validation | Existing, verification only: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | Use unchanged Node 20 installation, lint and test jobs; bind successful hosted results to the exact final PR head. |
| Evidence package | Proposed external execution artifacts, not application files | Preserve raw logs, fixture provenance, scan reports, complete comparison, PR/CI identity and actual usage under the original task. `proof/` paths below are intended paths relative to a durable evidence root outside `.axiom`, or attachment names, not proposed repository additions. |

## Interfaces and data

No application APIs, events, persistent schemas or migrations change. GET `/` retains dashboard rendering, service ordering and UTC freshness; `/api/promo-codes` retains its existing active-code behavior. `/health/live` remains independent of upstream probes. `/health/ready` returns 200 on success and 503 on upstream failure, connection error or timeout, returning to 200 after recovery. `/health/upstream` preserves its success payload and 502/error response. Existing metrics and promo-code assertions remain intact.

The regression component will exercise the proxy-addr implementation actually resolved by Express. Record that module resolution and its installed version rather than assuming a separately installed copy is representative. Prefer a direct dependency fixture with explicit trust configuration and request/address inputs. If verified advisory behavior requires Express request handling, use a separate test-only Express instance with local HTTP requests and lifecycle cleanup; never enable trust proxy on the exported application. This is a bounded fixture choice within the same four-case contract.

Each fixture records: stable case ID; advisory/reference origin; trust configuration; exact inputs; independent expected decision; and assertion rationale. S1 and S2 must exercise two evidence-backed security cases. C1 and C2 cover legitimate trusted and untrusted decisions. Expected results must not be computed by the function being tested or selected merely because versions differ. Exact payloads cannot be specified from the unverified references available in this stage. Establishing them is a prerequisite to implementation in UoW-2.

The vulnerable proof uses the baseline dependency graph plus the proposed test file, identified by its content digest. The fixed proof uses the identical test bytes and assertions with proxy-addr 2.0.8. No version-conditional expectations, expected-failure wrappers, skips or exclusions are allowed. A focused regression run is additional evidence; it does not replace the full suite.

Every execution evidence record identifies origin (baseline, vulnerable regression, fixed candidate or historical reference), revision, any test-only overlay, command, tool versions, timestamps, exit status, counts and durable artifact location. Preserve both successful and failing raw output. Candidate logs, CI and final scan must resolve to the same final head SHA. Any head movement requires refreshing affected proof before completion.

Scan records retain original OSV 2.6.0 reports and effective settings: all packages, no ignores and live API access. Compare complete inventories using ecosystem/package identity, package versions and advisory alias groups, preserving occurrence details. Report added, removed and retained findings; version changes must remain visible without confusing them with new advisory groups. Require the selected CVE/GHSA group to disappear, additions to be empty and the other 49 findings to remain explicitly listed as open. API failures, partial reports or unexplained inventory discrepancies cannot pass. Comparable scans close in time reduce live-data drift; repeat comparable captures if drift prevents a sound comparison.

If PR106 can be bound, validate that candidate after independently capturing the baseline and vulnerable proof. Otherwise create one workflow-required scoped PR referencing PR106 and record why reuse was unavailable.

## Units of work

These are cohesive slices within the original task, not replacement tickets. Sizes describe relative work, not observed token usage.

### UoW-1 — Capture baseline and establish evidence provenance — M

Delivers US-1 and the baseline portion of US-5; covers FR-1, FR-5, NFR-2 and NFR-3. No unit dependencies. Read the dependency files, application, five existing test files and CI configuration. Establish a durable evidence root and revision/tool record. Verify dashboard HTTP rendering and freshness, liveness independence during healthy/failing/pending upstream states, readiness success/failure/timeout/recovery, legacy upstream responses, metrics, promo-code cases and existing security floors. Preserve raw outputs and actual counts. A failed baseline or incomplete scan is an unresolved gate, not permission to suppress tests or expand remediation.

### UoW-2 — Establish and reproduce four security fixtures — L

Delivers US-2; covers FR-2, NFR-1 and NFR-3. Depends on UoW-1. Proposed component: `test/proxy-addr.test.js`; inspect dependency resolution and the application boundary. Read the advisory, release information and reference evidence during authorized execution, recording origins and distinguishing historical results. Establish S1/S2/C1/C2 with exact trust inputs and independently justified outcomes.

Run the four cases against installed 2.0.7. Require S1/S2 to fail their intended security assertions and C1/C2 to pass; import, network, timeout or setup failures do not qualify. Preserve fixture bytes/digest, dependency resolution and assertion output. Keep application trust proxy disabled. This is the riskiest unit because advisory details and release behavior are unverified: unsupported inputs or an incorrect target identity invalidate the core proof. Resolve mismatches before continuing rather than inventing a reproduction or claiming application exploitability.

### UoW-3 — Apply and validate the bounded upgrade — M

Delivers US-3; covers FR-2, FR-3, NFR-1, NFR-2 and NFR-3. Depends on UoW-2. Change `package-lock.json`, retain the four regression cases and change `package.json` only if strictly necessary. Verify installed and locked proxy-addr 2.0.8, including the copy resolved by Express. Run unchanged regression fixtures: four pass. Run lint and the complete suite under Node 20: 53 cases pass, comprising 49 existing and four new, with no failures, skips or exclusions. Review application behavior and default trust configuration. Lockfile churn or an unrelated dependency update fails the scope gate.

### UoW-4 — Bind the candidate and prove exact-head hosted CI — M

Delivers US-4; covers FR-4 and NFR-3. Depends on UoW-3. Use unchanged `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Prefer PR106 when the delivery workflow can bind it; otherwise create one scoped PR referencing PR106 and document that workflow requirement. Inspect the chosen candidate's actual diff, capture its final head SHA and rerun required proof for that candidate. Confirm hosted CI passes on that exact head, recording check URLs and SHA. Leave the PR open and unmerged. A changed head invalidates affected results and reopens validation.

### UoW-5 — Verify the complete vulnerability delta — M

Delivers US-5; covers FR-5, NFR-1 and NFR-3. Depends on UoW-1 and UoW-4. Scan the exact final head using OSV 2.6.0, all packages, no ignores, live API and settings comparable to the baseline. Preserve raw reports, commands, settings, timestamps and revisions. Compare every finding with package/version identities and alias groups. Require target removal, no additions and an explicit retained inventory of the other 49 open findings. Explain drift and discrepancies without silently changing scope or claiming completion. Unavailable APIs and incomplete reports remain failed verification gates.

### UoW-6 — Publish durable QA and actual usage — S

Delivers US-6; covers FR-6 and NFR-3. Depends on UoW-1 through UoW-5. Publish under the original task one short result table with exactly the rows Existing tests, Security regression, Full suite, CI, Rescan and Usage. Link full command logs, test counts, fixture proof, PR/CI URLs, final SHA, raw scans, full comparison and usage records. Keep operational prompts and intermediate logs outside the main description.

Follow every proof link and verify that candidate tests, hosted CI and the final scan identify the same final head. Upload evidence to Axiom attachments or preserve it outside `.axiom` and verify durable accessibility before completion. Distinguish actual fresh input tokens, output tokens and cost from the supplied 50–200k token estimate; identify planning usage separately against the up-to-$10 planning allowance. Missing usage accounting is an explicit completion gap, never an estimated result presented as actual.
